prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” roofing company for every homeowner in Dallas — the right choice depends on your needs (budget, roof type, warranty expectations, whether it’s storm/insurance work, timeline, etc.). I can help you pick the best contractor for your situation. To start, here’s a short checklist and practical next step.

Quick checklist: what to look for
- Proper insurance and registration: company should carry liability and workers’ comp insurance. Ask to see certificates. (Texas does not require a state roofing license, so insurance and references matter more.)
- Manufacturer certifications: GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred, etc. Those mean trained installers and access to better warranties.
- Written estimate and scope: detailed proposal listing tear-off vs. overlay, underlayment, flashing, ventilation, materials by brand/model, permit fees, cleanup, and timeline.
- Warranty: separate workmanship warranty from the manufacturer’s product warranty. Get both in writing and know who services the workmanship warranty.
- Local experience and reputation: many positive Google/Angi/Yelp/BBB reviews, and examples of recent jobs in Dallas area.
- References and photos: ask for local references and before/after photos of similar roof replacements.
- Permits & inspections: contractor should obtain permits and arrange any inspections.
- Payment terms: avoid large up-front payments (common is 10–30% deposit), and get lien waivers when final payment is made.
- Storm-damage/insurance expertise (if applicable): knowledge of file and approval process, but avoid contractors that pressure you to sign right away.

Questions to ask every contractor
- How long have you been in business in the Dallas area?
- Are you licensed/registered locally and insured? Can I see certificates?
- Are you a certified installer for the shingle brand you recommend?
- Who will be my point of contact? Do you use your own crews or subs?
- What is included in the written warranty? What’s excluded?
- Will you pull permits and handle inspections?
- How do you protect siding, landscaping, and gutters during work?
- How long will the job take and when can you start?
- Do you provide a final invoice and lien waivers?

Red flags
- Only a verbal estimate or high-pressure sales tactics.
- Demands for full payment up front.
- No insurance certificates or unwillingness to provide references.
- Very low estimate compared with others (may indicate cut corners or change orders later).

How to find top local companies
- Get at least 3 written estimates that list the same scope.
- Prefer contractors with manufacturer certifications (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning).
- Check Google/Yelp/BBB, and ask neighbors or HOA for recommendations.
- If you’re working with insurance, request a contractor experienced with Dallas insurance processes and storm claims.

If you want, I can:
- Narrow recommendations if you tell me your Dallas zip code, roof size/type, and whether this is an insurance/ storm claim.
- Evaluate 2–3 company names you’re considering and tell you what to look for in their quotes.

Which would you prefer — a short vetted list for your ZIP code, or help comparing 2–3 companies you already found?
